title: Shortest paths without weights
summary: Use BFS distances and parent pointers to find the fewest-edges route.
hints: BFS already knows the distance: when you discover `v` from `u`, `dist[v] = dist[u] + 1`. Start with `std::vector<int> dist(g.size(), -1)`; `-1` doubles as the 'not visited' marker, so you do not need a separate visited array.
For `shortest_path`, run the same BFS but also record `parent[v] = u` at the moment you discover `v`. You can stop early once `target` is discovered.

To rebuild the path, walk backwards from `target` following `parent[]` until you reach `start`, pushing each vertex, then `std::reverse` the result. Handle `start == target` (path is just `{start}`) and an unreachable target (return an empty vector).
